target.title: fix(auto-reply): include peer-scoped key in browser tab cleanup on /new
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/new` and `/reset` can leave browser tabs open for direct-message sessions. Those tabs are tracked under the peer-scoped runtime-policy key, while reset cleanup previously looked up only the canonical session key and previous session UUID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset boundary now derives the same runtime-policy session key used when browser tabs are registered and includes it in the exact cleanup-key set. The browser registry remains exact-keyed: no fuzzy matching, agent-wide close, or cross-peer fallback.

The maintainer refinement keeps the existing canonical key and previous session UUID for their established cleanup cases, reuses the existing key resolver, and adds a regression proving the complete key set.

## User Impact

Resetting a direct-message session closes that peer's managed browser tabs. Tabs belonging to another peer remain open. Existing canonical-session and prior-session cleanup continue unchanged.

## Evidence

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, original contributor head `5f47a55385b5b3a0b84f21f7d70d2598fc9eea69`: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` — 115/115 passed (`run_c2a250f5754e`).
- Blacksmith Testbox, current-main plus the refined patch: the focused session suite passed 134/134; targeted `oxfmt --check` passed; full `pnpm build` passed (lease `tbx_01kwv4e6gzbxhajdtyrhfzrh5a`).
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox, rewritten PR head `7d541c9aeabf7b4c5a4ef60a392134dac903b4cc`: exact SHA verified, public networking/no Tailscale/no instance role, full `pnpm build` passed (`run_2263009c1d63`).
- CI on the rewritten two-file head: build, lint, production/test types, security boundaries, plugin contracts, and all relevant compact shards passed. Two whole-repository shards failed in unrelated current-main/stale-head surfaces; the branch will be brought current before landing.
- A final Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + managed Chromium proof is being run before merge and will be posted with the exact run ID and peer-isolation result.

## Trust Boundary

Direct-message browser ownership remains per resolved runtime-policy peer key. Reset cleanup receives that exact peer key; it does not broaden cleanup to the agent or canonical-session namespace. The regression asserts the old UUID, canonical key, and peer-scoped key explicitly.

## Linked Context

No linked issue.
